q: What is meant by Materials-at-Site (MAS) in railway stores accounts?

options.A: Stock lying in the divisional stores depot
options.B: Materials issued from the depot but lying unused at the work site
options.C: Materials under inspection at the supplier's premises

q: Who is responsible for the custody of materials lying at a work site?
To which account are materials debited when issued from the depot to a work site?

options.A: The work for which they are issued

q: What does the MAS ledger maintained at the site record?

options.A: Only issues made from the depot
options.D: Receipts, consumption and balances of materials at site

q: How are Materials-at-Site returns rendered by the engineer?

options.B: Periodically, showing receipts, consumption and balance
options.C: Only on completion of the work

q: How are MAS balances checked against the records?

options.A: By physical verification and reconciliation with the MAS ledger
options.C: Only at the final bill stage

q: What happens to MAS when the engineer-in-charge of a work is transferred?

options.A: It automatically reverts to the depot
options.B: It is written off the books
options.C: It is handed over to the relieving engineer after joint verification
options.D: It is auctioned at the site

q: How is surplus MAS disposed of on completion of a work?

options.A: It is left at the site
options.B: It is distributed among the staff
options.D: It is returned to the depot and credited to the work

q: How is a shortage of MAS found during verification dealt with?

options.B: It is investigated and adjusted under competent sanction
options.C: It is automatically charged to the contractor
options.D: It is added back to depot stock

q: Materials lying at site remain the property of whom until consumed?

options.A: The railway, until consumed in the work

q: What is the position of materials issued to a contractor for a departmental work?

options.B: They need not be accounted for
options.C: They are accounted for and the contractor is answerable for custody and surplus
options.D: They are issued free of charge

q: When is consumption of MAS recorded in the site accounts?

options.A: On the date of issue from the depot
options.C: When the contractor's bill is passed
options.D: As materials are actually consumed in the work

q: When is the MAS account of a work finally closed?

options.A: At the end of every month
options.B: On completion of the work after adjusting surplus and shortages
options.D: At the time of the budget

q: How is unserviceable material found at the site dealt with?

options.A: It is surveyed and disposed of as scrap under the rules
options.B: It is buried at the site
options.C: It is returned to the supplier
options.D: It is thrown away without record

q: Reconciliation of MAS involves comparing which two records?

options.C: Site ledger balances with depot issue vouchers

q: How is MAS reflected in the works accounts until consumed?

options.D: In the work's account as materials at site until consumed

q: What is the procedure if MAS is stolen from the site?

options.A: The engineer pays for it from his pocket automatically
options.B: The loss is reported, investigated and written off under competent sanction

q: How are materials returned from the site to the depot treated?

options.A: Taken on stock by the depot and the work credited with their value

q: What is the engineer-in-charge required to ensure regarding MAS?

options.B: That it is mixed with the contractor's own material
options.C: That it is properly stored, safeguarded and accounted for
options.D: That it is always left in the open

q: By whom are MAS balances verified?

options.D: Jointly by engineering and accounts or stores representatives

q: How does Materials-at-Site differ from materials on hand?

options.A: They are exactly the same thing
options.B: MAS is issued material lying at the work site, while materials on hand are unissued depot stock
options.D: Materials on hand are kept at the work site

q: Which document supports the issue of materials from the depot to a work site?

options.A: Issue notes or vouchers from the depot

q: What should be done about MAS not consumed within a reasonable time?

options.A: It may lie at site indefinitely
options.C: It should be reviewed and the surplus returned to the depot

q: At what value is MAS accounted for in the work's account?

options.A: At the prevailing market rate at site
options.D: At the issue rate at which it was debited to the work

q: In departmental execution, MAS at the site is in the custody of whom?

options.B: The site engineer under the engineer-in-charge

q: What is required to transfer MAS from one work to another?

options.A: Sanction with transfer vouchers debiting the receiving work and crediting the issuing work

q: The MAS statement is reconciled with which accounts record?

options.C: The expenditure booked to the work in the divisional accounts

q: How is pilferage of MAS at the site handled?

options.C: It is charged to the depot
options.D: It is reported and investigated, with the loss regularized under sanction

q: What does the final MAS account of a completed work show?

options.A: A large surplus in all cases
options.B: Nil balance, with all material consumed, returned or adjusted
options.D: The same balance as at the start

q: Where is the MAS ledger kept?

options.A: At the site, with returns rendered to the depot or divisional office

q: What is the effect of issuing materials to a site in excess of requirement?

options.B: It earns interest for the railway
options.C: It should be avoided and the excess returned to the depot
options.D: Excess material is free of cost

q: Who signs the MAS physical verification report?
How must cement lying at a work site be stored?

options.B: Stored under cover on raised platforms to prevent damage

q: How should steel materials at a work site be kept?

options.A: Stacked properly and safeguarded against corrosion and theft

q: What happens to MAS of a work that is closed or abandoned?

options.A: It is abandoned at the site
options.C: It is returned to the depot and credited to the work

q: To which account is the cost of watch and ward of MAS charged?
How are materials issued to contractors for railway works treated in accounts?

options.B: Debited to the work, with the contractor accountable for custody and consumption
options.C: Treated as a free gift to the contractor

q: What must the measurement of work done tally with?

options.A: Materials consumed as per the MAS records

q: How is a discrepancy between the MAS ledger and the physical balance treated?

options.A: It is erased from the ledger
options.C: It is investigated and regularized under competent sanction

q: What is the purpose of rendering MAS returns?

options.B: To delay the progress of works
options.D: To exercise control over materials and prevent misuse

q: Which materials are included under Materials-at-Site?

options.B: All stores issued from the depot lying unused at the work site

q: What is the issue rate used for valuing MAS?

options.A: The depot issue or book rate at which the material was issued
options.D: An arbitrary rate fixed by the engineer

q: How is surplus cement at a site handled on completion of the work?

options.C: Returned to the depot or transferred to another work under sanction

q: What must the engineer avoid doing with railway MAS?

options.D: Mixing railway materials with the contractor's own materials

q: How is the MAS account maintained for different works?
When is physical verification of MAS carried out?

options.A: Periodically and whenever charge of the work changes

q: How is MAS shortage due to natural causes like evaporation treated?

options.C: Treated as unavoidable loss and written off under competent sanction

q: Who bears the risk of loss of MAS lying at site?

options.D: The railway bears its own risk and safeguards it by watch and ward

q: What must happen to MAS before the final bill of a work is settled?

options.B: It must be fully accounted for through consumption, return or adjustment

q: Where are depot issues to a work site recorded?

options.A: In depot issue vouchers and the site MAS receipt records

q: What is the effect of drawing materials well in advance of requirement?

options.C: It locks up capital in MAS and should be avoided
options.D: Advance drawal is free of cost

q: How are rails and sleepers kept at the site of track works?

options.D: Stacked in measured stacks and accounted for

q: On what basis is a further installment of material released to a site?

options.B: Regulated with reference to consumption of earlier issues

q: How is MAS damaged by floods or natural calamity dealt with?

options.A: Surveyed, with the loss reported and regularized under sanction

q: What details does the MAS ledger show?

options.C: Date-wise receipts, consumption and balances quantity-wise

q: What happens if a contractor fails to return surplus MAS?

options.D: Its value is recovered from the contractor's dues at prescribed rates

q: What is the nature of MAS lying at the site of a work in progress?

options.B: It is an asset of the railway held at site until consumed

q: What does physical verification of MAS involve?

options.A: Actual counting, measuring or weighing of materials at site
options.B: Reading depot files in the office

q: How long must MAS records be preserved?

options.C: Until final closure of the work's accounts and completion of audit

q: What is the main objective of MAS accounting?

options.D: To ensure every material issued to a work is consumed, returned or accounted for
